nodes.title: Prevent GitHub actions from running on forks
nodes.body:
### Confirmation

- [x] I am a [maintainer](https://github.com/orgs/electron/people) of the Electron project. (If not, please create a [different issue type](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/new/).)

### Description

I've received a report where our GitHub actions (builds, stable prep, etc.) were running on someone's fork.

We should prevent that from happening. It can cost people money.

We [fixed it](https://github.com/electron/website/pull/915) for the website repo by disabling GitHub actions for all forks (see also [this Slack discussion](https://electronhq.slack.com/archives/CNTJBD467/p1762274100799969)).

nodes.title: When first calling dialog.showSaveDialog, default to downloads/documents
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

When calling `dialog.showSaveDialog` for the first time on windows, it opens to the current working directory. This is definitely not where users want to save files.

Windows version tested: Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 26100.6899 x64, macOS Tahoe

### Proposed Solution

Save the last location as normal. If there's no existing saved location, default to something like the user's downloads directory, documents directory, or even their desktop. On linux, the user's home directory is a good default.

FYI, on windows server there's no downloads directory.

### Alternatives Considered

Each application developer could solve this by providing/saving their own download locations.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Type error with latest @types/node v22/24
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Type check should pass with latest `@types/node` versions.
The following should have no errors:
```
mkdir electron-type-error
cd electron-type-error
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm i typescript electron
npx tsc --init --skipLibCheck false
echo "import electron from 'electron'; console.log(electron.shell);" > main.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
```

### Actual Behavior

Fails as of `@types/node@22.19.3` with:
```
node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712:17 - error TS2687: All declarations of 'noDeprecation' must have identical modifiers.

1712                 noDeprecation?: boolean;
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~

node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712:17 - error TS2717: Subsequent property declarations must have the same type.  Property 'noDeprecation' must be of type 'boolean', but here has type 'boolean | undefined'.

1712                 noDeprecation?: boolean;
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738:5
    25738     noDeprecation: boolean;
              ~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    'noDeprecation' was also declared here.

node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738:5 - error TS2687: All declarations of 'noDeprecation' must have identical modifiers.

25738     noDeprecation: boolean;
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~


Found 3 errors in 2 files.

Errors  Files
     2  node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712
     1  node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738

```

Seems like @types/node [added](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/pull/74184) `noDeprecation` as an optional field, but electron defines it as required.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Not sure where the type is actually defined in electron. I see there's https://github.com/electron/typescript-definitions, but which api .json is it given?

nodes.title: Crash on startup with Electron 40.x built with v8_enable_sandbox=false (Illegal Access in IndirectBaseHandle::IsEmpty)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 26100

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.2.6

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior


When built with the following flags:
```
  v8_enable_sandbox = false
  v8_enable_pointer_compression = false
```
The application should start normally (same behavior as with my custom 39.2.6 build with the same flags).

### Actual Behavior

Electron 40.x crashes on startup (Apparently this only happens on Windows).

`Unhandled error in main process: Error: ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'http://localhost:8100'
    at rejectAndCleanup (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:83298)
    at finishListener (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:83460)
    at WebContents.stopLoadingListener (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:83847)
    at WebContents.emit (node:events:508:28)
    at WebContents.emit (node:domain:489:12) {
  errno: -2,
  code: 'ERR_FAILED',
  url: 'http://localhost:8100'`

Crash dump points to an Illegal Access Exception at IndirectBaseHandle::IsEmpty in v8-handle-base.h.





### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Steps to reproduce**

Clone Electron source for 40.0.0-beta.X.

Configure GN with:
```
  v8_enable_sandbox = false
  v8_enable_pointer_compression = false
```
  
Build Electron (e.g. ninja -C out/Release electron).

Run my app with the newly built Electron.

The app immediately fails to boot; main process throws the ERR_FAILED (-2) error, and the minidump shows an Illegal Access in IndirectBaseHandle::IsEmpty.

[4fcd5d3e-4d1a-4e01-b906-71bf6080c7b4.dmp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24119662/4fcd5d3e-4d1a-4e01-b906-71bf6080c7b4.dmp)

**Prebuilt files and pdbs**
https://we.tl/t-ubFTLtdMhz

nodes.title: Change to gin_converters/guid_converter broke UUID sanitation
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

v41.0.0-nightly.20251210, 36.9.5

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows, macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS Tahoe, Win11, Win10

### What arch are you using?

Other (specify below)

### Last Known Working Electron version

36.7.4

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon`  should be able to take in a guid of format `{<guid>}` in addition to `<guid>`

Root cause is in additional information

### Actual Behavior

when passing a guid into `NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon` of the format `{<guid>}`, it errors out with `Invalid GUID format - GUID must be a string`

Root cause is in additional information

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/a0d983e4b53432b236499cf76638ead4dd3d2c46 added a change where `NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon` takes in a base::Uuid GUID as opposed to a UUID GUID.

The gin_converter/guid_converter for UUID GUID has input sanitization that removes { & } from the outside of the GUID presumably because Windows tends to wrap in guids in braces
```
if (!guid.empty()) {
      if (guid[0] == '{' && guid[guid.length() - 1] == '}') {
        guid = guid.substr(1, guid.length() - 2);
      }
    }
```

Since we switched to using a base::Uuid GUID, & its gin converter does not have this input sanitization, existing electron users that take in a guid of the format `{ guid }` are met with an error `Invalid GUID format - GUID must be a string` because the converter returns an empty string.

### Expected Behavior

A `BrowserWindow` with a specified `titleBarOverlay` will position the traffic lights differently when calling `setWindowButtonPosition()` from an otherwise identical `BrowserWindow` which has no `tileBarOverlay`.

The presence of a `titleBarOverlay` in the options should not affect the way the traffic light position is calculated when calling `setWindowButtonPosition`.

### Additional Information

I tested in electron versions 38 and 39 and the issue is present, it seems to work fine in 37. Additionally, this doesn't seem to manifest in macOS Sequoia.

Windows

### Operating System Version

10.0.26200.7462

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

38.2.2

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

We expect to be able to resize the window if "resizable: true" is set and this should not depend from the other options like "frame", "transparent", etc.

### Actual Behavior

If we specify:
```
frame: false,
transparent: true,
resizable: true
```
in BrowserWindowConstructorOptions, the window can't be resized nor resize cursor appears.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/estoykov/5c0f777ce24df8c7c7a204d53ab732cc

### Additional Information

May be with this PR https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48499 if we create frameless, transparent window it can not be resized, even if we set "resizable: true" in constructor options.
You can use the provided gist to check with the latest stable Electrons and with 38.2.2.
It is just the standard Electron app with few options added:
```
const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    transparent: true,
    frame: false,
    resizable: true,
    backgroundColor: "gray",
    webPreferences: {
      preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js')
    }
  })
```

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 ,Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When launching an Electron app with GPU enabled, the render process should start successfully regardless of whether the app is running with normal or administrator privileges.

### Actual Behavior

When running the app as Administrator, the render process fails immediately with the following error:
`render-process-gone { reason: "launch-failed', exitCode: 18 }`
If the same app is run with normal user privileges, it starts correctly.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Adding the no-sandbox and disable-gpu-sandbox options at startup makes the app work even under Administrator mode. This indicates that the issue is likely related to Electron’s sandbox implementation conflicting with elevated permissions. Not all machines reproduce the issue, only certain Windows configurations with GPU enabled.

Adding app.commandLine.appendSwitch('no-sandbox') or app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-gpu-sandbox') makes the app work even under Administrator mode.

Not all machines reproduce the issue, only certain Windows configurations with GPU enabled.
